newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil trade gap to rise in '97 -- Banco de Boston.
newsitem.headline: Brazil trade gap to rise in '97 -- Banco de Boston.

text.p: Brazil is likely to post a $7.0 billion trade deficit in 1997, against $4.5-$5 billion this year, said Banco de Boston President Carlos Craide.
"This year's trade deficit will be near $4.5 billion and $5 billion, and may grow to $7 billion in 1997," he told reporters.
Craide said the expected higher 1997 deficit is not worrisome as it is significantly small compared with gross domestic product and is easily financed by foreign direct investment.
"What is important is how the trade and current account deficits are financed," he said.
Craide said foreign direct investment in 1996 is expected to reach $8 billion, representing almost 40 percent of the country's three percent current account gap.
He also said Brazil will experience a wave of big privatizations next year, which will help increase investments in the country.
"Next year foreign direct investment will top $10 billion," he said.

Even congressional opposition to the selloff of mining firm Companhia Vale do Rio Doce, scheduled to begin in February, is not expected to take the shine off Brazil's privatization program, according to Craide.
"If Vale's privatization did not take place, it would not be a chaos," he said, noting power and telecommunications privatizations will attract massive investments next year.
Craide took over as president of Bank of Boston Corp's Brazil unit early in October, succeeding Henrique Meirelles, who became Bank of Boston Corp president and chief operating officer.
